newsitem.title: USA: News Corp. to buy Heritage Media.
newsitem.headline: News Corp. to buy Heritage Media.

text.p: Rupert Murdoch's News Corp. Ltd said on Monday it reached an agreement to buy marketing company Heritage Media Corp. for stock valued at about $754 million.
News Corp. said it planned to sell Heritage's radio and television broadcast properties and keep its marketing services operations, which would complement those of its own.
Heritage, based in Dallas, provides in-store marketing products and services for grocery, drug and mass merchandise outlets.
"Heritage's marketing services operations are a great complement to our existing FSI (free standing inserts) business," Murdoch said said in a statement.
Heritage also operates six network-affiliated television stations and 24 radio stations in seven major markets.
News Corp. said it was making the acquisition through a subsidiary and would pay the equivalent of $20.50 for each of Heritage's 38.6 million shares.
It said it also will assume Heritage's outstanding debt of about $600 million.
Heritage's shares closed Friday at $12.125 and News Corp.'s American Depositary Receipts closed at $20.875, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
The transaction is subject to the approvals of the Heritage shareholders and regulatory agencies.

Heritage owns ACTMEDIA Inc., which provides in-store marketing products in more than 40,000 supermarkets, drug stores and mass merchandisers worldwide, and DIMAC Marketing Corp., a full-service, vertically integrated direct marketing services company.

News Corp., through its U.S. division, News America FSI, publishes free-standing promotional inserts in the United States. It produces more than 60 million weekly inserts, which are distributed in more than 600 Sunday newspapers throughout the country.
